Implementation: Centralize User Visibility Setup

Summary

Added ResolveUserVisibility to the global Functions utility and routed six matching flows through it. The utility shares the existing visibility implementation while intentionally skipping blocked-post loading.

Changes

Functions.go

Added:

func ResolveUserVisibility(c *fiber.Ctx, role, encrypt, lastLogin string) ContentVisibility

ResolveContentVisibility and ResolveUserVisibility now call one internal implementation:

func resolveVisibility(c *fiber.Ctx, role, encrypt, lastLogin string, includeBlockedPosts bool) ContentVisibility
  • ResolveContentVisibility passes true and retains its blocked-post behavior.
  • ResolveUserVisibility passes false and does not access the blocked-post Redis key.

Updated flows

  • TotalBlockedComment.go
  • TotalBlockedLikeComment.go
  • TotalBlockedLikePost.go
  • TotalBlockProfileUser.go
  • GetPlaceList.go
  • PlaceDetailRequest.go

The handlers now consume:

visibility := Functions.ResolveUserVisibility(c, role, encrypt, lastLogin)
if visibility.Unauthorized {
	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")
}
lastLogin = visibility.LastLogin
notInEncrypt := visibility.ExcludedUsers

PlaceDetailRequest.go maps the same result into its existing package-local placeDetailRequest. Its four callers and their validation order remain unchanged.

TotalBlockedComment.go retains role, type, and SID validation before visibility loading. TotalBlockProfileUser.go retains target-user lookup before visibility loading. GetPlaceList.go retains parameter, category, and role validation before visibility loading.

Shared Flow

ResolveUserVisibility performs the matching operations in this order:

  1. Preserve the caller-provided default lastLogin.
  2. Reject roles other than user and viewer.
  3. Load deactivated users.
  4. Return immediately for a viewer.
  5. Load authenticated user data for a user.
  6. Return unauthorized state when user data is invalid.
  7. Replace lastLogin with the stored value.
  8. Load blocked users.
  9. Append blocked users after deactivated users.

Blocked posts are not loaded by this entry point.

Compatibility

  • Existing ResolveContentVisibility behavior and Redis lookup order remain unchanged.
  • User-only flows retain the same deactivated-user and blocked-user keys.
  • ExcludedUsers remains []string; no conversion to []interface{} was introduced.
  • Viewer requests still use only deactivated-user exclusions.
  • User requests still use the stored last_login and both user-exclusion sources.
  • No database query, selected column, join, filter, ordering, pagination, counter, or scan model changed.
  • No response key, value, type, nullability, status code, message, or error changed.
  • Encryption input, ls, and viewer e4 behavior remain unchanged.
  • No mobile-facing API contract changed.

Test-Driven Verification

Added TestResolveUserVisibilityRejectsInvalidRoleBeforeDependencies before production code. Its first focused run failed with:

undefined: ResolveUserVisibility

After implementation, the focused utility and affected package tests passed.

Verification

go test -count=1 ./src/Utils/Functions ./src/Action/V1/Places ./src/Action/V1/Comments ./src/Action/V1/Likes ./src/Action/V1/Users
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • Focused package tests pass.
  • Complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Scope Audit

  • One global utility entry point added.
  • One focused utility test added.
  • Six matching flows updated.
  • The existing Place Detail adapter retained.
  • Endpoint-specific queries and responses remain in their handlers.
  • No dependency, configuration, route, model, schema, Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated handler changed.
  • The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Problem

Six related flows repeated the same visibility setup without blocked-post filtering:

  • TotalBlockedComment.go
  • TotalBlockedLikeComment.go
  • TotalBlockedLikePost.go
  • TotalBlockProfileUser.go
  • GetPlaceList.go
  • PlaceDetailRequest.go, which serves four Place Detail handlers

Each flow validates the user or viewer role, loads deactivated users, resolves authenticated user data and last_login, loads blocked users, and combines the same user-exclusion list. The same behavior already existed beside ResolveContentVisibility, except these flows must not load blocked posts.

Scope

  • Add a reusable user-only visibility entry point in src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go.
  • Share the existing visibility implementation without loading blocked posts.
  • Update all six matching flows to consume the utility.
  • Keep PlaceDetailRequest.go as the adapter for its four existing callers.
  • Remove imports and local variables superseded by the utility.
  • Keep endpoint-specific validation, queries, counters, response shaping, and encryption in their existing files.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Accepted roles: user and viewer only.
  • Existing HTTP 401 response structure and message for invalid roles or invalid user data.
  • Each flow's existing validation and utility-call position.
  • Deactivated-user Redis key <prefix>_deactive_users_ec.
  • Blocked-user Redis key <prefix>_blocked_users_ec_<encrypt>.
  • Lookup order: deactivated users, authenticated user data, then blocked users.
  • No blocked-post Redis lookup.
  • Deactivated users before blocked users in the exclusion list.
  • Viewer behavior without authenticated user-data or blocked-user lookups.
  • Existing last_login and default timestamp behavior.
  • Existing SQL queries, filters, projections, ordering, pagination, counters, and scan models.
  • Existing response keys, values, types, status codes, messages, errors, and encryption.

Out of Scope

  • Changing endpoint-specific database queries or selected columns.
  • Combining the six handlers beyond their matching visibility setup.
  • Changing Redis decoding, keys, or fallback behavior.
  • Changing API response contracts or mobile compatibility.
  • Removing the Place Detail adapter or modifying its four callers.
  • Refactoring Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated handlers.

Acceptance Criteria

  • ResolveUserVisibility exists as a global utility.
  • It reuses the existing visibility implementation without loading blocked posts.
  • All six matching flows use the utility.
  • Invalid roles return before Redis or Fiber-dependent user-data access.
  • Viewer and user lookup behavior remains unchanged.
  • Query, response, encryption, and error behavior remains unchanged.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • Focused package tests pass.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-09. No commit was created.

Implementation: Centralize Visibility Redundancy Refactor

Summary

Centralized content and user visibility resolution across 23 action files by utilizing ResolveContentVisibility and ResolveUserVisibility in src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go. Eliminated hundreds of lines of duplicate Redis lookups, user data fetching, role checks, and error handling. Files relating to slim, sl, or worker were strictly left untouched.

Changes

1. src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go & Functions_test.go

  • Extended ContentVisibility to expose identity fields and distinct blocked users slice:
type ContentVisibility struct {
	UserId        string
	Email         string
	LastLogin     string
	BlockedPosts  []string
	BlockedUsers  []string
	ExcludedUsers []string
	Unauthorized  bool
}
  • Enhanced internal helper resolveVisibility:
func resolveVisibility(c *fiber.Ctx, role, encrypt, lastLogin string, includeBlockedPosts bool) ContentVisibility {
	visibility := ContentVisibility{LastLogin: lastLogin}
	if role != "user" && role != "viewer" {
		visibility.Unauthorized = true
		return visibility
	}

	ctx := context.Background()
	deactivatedUsers := Redis.GetEncodedStringList(ctx, Config.Prefix+"_deactive_users_ec")
	visibility.ExcludedUsers = deactivatedUsers
	if role == "viewer" {
		return visibility
	}

	userData := UserFunctions.UserDatas(c, encrypt)
	if userData["status"] == "error" {
		visibility.Unauthorized = true
		return visibility
	}

	if userId, ok := userData["user_id"].(string); ok {
		visibility.UserId = userId
	}
	if email, ok := userData["email"].(string); ok {
		visibility.Email = email
	}
	visibility.LastLogin = userData["last_login"].(string)
	if includeBlockedPosts {
		visibility.BlockedPosts = Redis.GetEncodedStringList(ctx, Config.Prefix+"_blocked_post_ec_"+encrypt)
	}
	blockedUsers := Redis.GetEncodedStringList(ctx, Config.Prefix+"_blocked_users_ec_"+encrypt)
	visibility.BlockedUsers = blockedUsers
	visibility.ExcludedUsers = append(deactivatedUsers, blockedUsers...)

	return visibility
}
  • Added unit tests in Functions_test.go verifying that UserId, Email, BlockedUsers, BlockedPosts, and ExcludedUsers remain clean on invalid role rejection before any Redis or Fiber dependencies are touched.

2. Action Handlers Refactored

Replaced duplicated Redis and user lookup boilerplate with ResolveContentVisibility or ResolveUserVisibility across:

    • src/Action/V1/Affiliate/ListAffiliate.go -> Uses ResolveUserVisibility, extracts UserId, LastLogin.

  • Bookmarks:

    • src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/PublishedFolderRequest.go -> Uses ResolveContentVisibility.

  • Broadcast:

    • src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListPotdBroadcast.go -> Uses ResolveUserVisibility, extracts UserId, Email, ExcludedUsers.

  • Collection Post:

  • Comments:

    • src/Action/V1/Comments/ListComments.go -> Uses ResolveContentVisibility, checks blocked post slug.
    • src/Action/V1/Comments/ListRepliesComment.go -> Uses ResolveContentVisibility, checks blocked post slug.
    • src/Action/V1/Comments/TotalBlockedComment.go -> Uses ResolveUserVisibility.
    • src/Action/V1/Comments/TotalBlockedLikeComment.go -> Uses ResolveUserVisibility.

  • Hashtags:

    • src/Action/V1/Hashtag/SearchHashtag.go -> Uses ResolveContentVisibility.

  • Likes:

    • src/Action/V1/Likes/CheckLikePost.go -> Uses ResolveContentVisibility.
    • src/Action/V1/Likes/ListProfileLikedPosts.go -> Uses ResolveUserVisibility.
    • src/Action/V1/Likes/TotalBlockedLikePost.go -> Uses ResolveUserVisibility.

  • Places:

    • src/Action/V1/Places/GetPlaceList.go -> Uses ResolveUserVisibility.
    • src/Action/V1/Places/PlaceDetailRequest.go -> Uses ResolveUserVisibility.

  • Posts:

    • src/Action/V1/Posts/NearestPost.go -> Uses ResolveContentVisibility.
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/NearestPostForViewsPanorama.go -> Uses ResolveContentVisibility.
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/PostAgg.go -> Uses ResolveContentVisibility.
    • src/Action/V2/Posts/DetailPost.go -> Uses ResolveContentVisibility.

  • Recommendations:

    • src/Action/V1/Recommendations/PopularPosts.go -> Uses ResolveContentVisibility.

  • Search:

    • src/Action/V1/Search/SearchPost.go -> Uses ResolveContentVisibility.

  • Users:

    • src/Action/V1/Users/TotalBlockProfileUser.go -> Uses ResolveUserVisibility.

3. Cleanup

  • Removed unused package imports (context, Redis, UserFunctions, Config) where no longer needed by handler files.
  • Removed unused local variable allocations (deactiveUser, blockUser, etc.).

Verification

Run all test suites and compilation checks:

go build ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All unit and integration test packages pass.
  • No files relating to slim, sl, or worker were altered.

Problem

Multiple endpoint action files across V1 and V2 repeated boilerplate logic for user authentication, role validation, deactivated user lookup, user data retrieval, and Redis blocked user/post filtering:

  • src/Action/V1/Affiliate/ListAffiliate.go
  • src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/PublishedFolderRequest.go
  • src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListBroadcast.go
  • src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListPotdBroadcast.go
  • src/Action/V1/CollectionPost/CollectionPostDetail.go
  • src/Action/V1/Comments/ListComments.go
  • src/Action/V1/Comments/ListRepliesComment.go
  • src/Action/V1/Comments/TotalBlockedComment.go
  • src/Action/V1/Comments/TotalBlockedLikeComment.go
  • src/Action/V1/Hashtag/SearchHashtag.go
  • src/Action/V1/Likes/CheckLikePost.go
  • src/Action/V1/Likes/ListProfileLikedPosts.go
  • src/Action/V1/Likes/TotalBlockedLikePost.go
  • src/Action/V1/Places/GetPlaceList.go

  • src/Action/V1/Posts/NearestPostForViewsPanorama.go
  • src/Action/V1/Posts/PostAgg.go
  • src/Action/V1/Recommendations/PopularPosts.go

Each file was manually connecting to Redis, fetching deactivated user lists (_deactive_users_ec), calling UserFunctions.UserDatas, querying blocked posts (_blocked_post_ec_<encrypt>) and blocked users (_blocked_users_ec_<encrypt>), and handling repetitive error checks. This led to high maintenance overhead and duplicated logic across the codebase.

Scope

  • Extend ContentVisibility struct in src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go to include UserId, Email, and BlockedUsers for handlers that require identity attributes alongside visibility lists.
  • Consolidate common resolution inside resolveVisibility(c *fiber.Ctx, role, encrypt, lastLogin string, includeBlockedPosts bool).
  • Use ResolveContentVisibility in handlers requiring blocked post exclusions and user exclusions.
  • Use ResolveUserVisibility in handlers requiring only user exclusions (deactivated + blocked users) without blocked posts.
  • Remove redundant imports (context, Redis, UserFunctions, Config) and local variables from refactored handler files.
  • Strictly exclude any file related to slim, sl, or worker from changes.
  • Maintain existing endpoint behavior, SQL queries, HTTP status codes, error messages, and response contracts.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Allowed roles (user, viewer) and unauthorized status code (401).
  • Redis key structure: <prefix>_deactive_users_ec, <prefix>_blocked_users_ec_<encrypt>, and <prefix>_blocked_post_ec_<encrypt>.
  • Resolution order: validate role -> load deactivated users -> short-circuit viewer -> load user data -> load blocked posts/users -> combine exclusion list.
  • Timestamp format and default lastLogin handling.
  • Existing database queries, joins, filters, ordering, pagination, and response mapping.
  • Existing encryption (EncryptSuccessResult, EncryptResult, ls, and viewer e4) behavior.
  • Zero touch on files with slim, sl, or worker in name/purpose.

Out of Scope

  • Changing database schema, table joins, or column selections.
  • Changing API response structures, error message phrasing, or status codes.
  • Auto-committing or pushing git changes.

Acceptance Criteria

  • ContentVisibility struct safely exposes UserId, Email, BlockedUsers, BlockedPosts, ExcludedUsers, LastLogin, and Unauthorized.
  • All candidate action files use ResolveContentVisibility or ResolveUserVisibility instead of duplicated manual Redis/UserData calls.
  • Redundant imports and local variables are cleaned up.
  • No files relating to slim, sl, or worker are touched.
  • Unit and integration tests pass: go test -count=1 ./src/....
  • go build ./... succeeds with zero errors.

Implementation: Centralize Pagination Usage

Summary

Standardized pagination parameter handling across 9 non-slim action handlers by adopting Functions.Pagination(c, defaultLimit). Replaced repeated manual c.QueryInt, default fallback checks, and offset arithmetic with a single idiomatic helper call. Files relating to slim, sl, or worker were strictly excluded.

Changes

Replaced manual pagination blocks:

page := c.QueryInt("page")
limit := c.QueryInt("limit")

if page == 0 {
    page = 1
}

if limit == 0 {
    limit = defaultLimit
}

offset := (page * limit) - limit

with the unified helper call:

_, limit, offset := Functions.Pagination(c, defaultLimit)

Problem

Multiple V1 endpoint action files manually parsed pagination query parameters (page, limit) and calculated the database offset using repetitive boilerplate:

Implementation: Centralize Profile Follower Flow

Summary

Consolidated the duplicated Profile Follower and Search Profile Follower behavior into one canonical flow in the Users package (ProfileFollower.go). The Search package now delegates to UsersAction.SearchProfileFollower(c), eliminating nearly 190 lines of duplicate code. A boolean parameter enables search-specific parameter parsing and SQL predicates.

Changes

1. src/Action/V1/Users/ProfileFollower.go

  • The existing entry point now calls the shared flow without search behavior:
func ProfileFollower(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
	return profileFollower(c, false)
}
  • Added the search entry point:
func SearchProfileFollower(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
	return profileFollower(c, true)
}
  • Added profileFollower(c *fiber.Ctx, search bool) error, which unifies request validation, user lookup, visibility checks, follower query, followed-state lookup, response shaping, and encryption.
  • Decodes usernameFullname only when search is true.
  • Fixed the previous uninitialized encrypt check when verifying blocked users.
  • Added query helper:
func profileFollowerQuery(db *gorm.DB, userID, search string, searchEnabled bool) *gorm.DB {
	query := db.Table("followers").
		Select("followers.follower_id, users.fullname, users.username, users.avatar, users.encrypt").
		Joins("INNER JOIN users ON followers.follower_id = users.id").
		Where("followers.user_id = ?", userID)

	if searchEnabled {
		query = query.Where("users.username ILIKE ? OR users.fullname ILIKE ?", "%"+search+"%", "%"+search+"%")
	}

	return query.Where("users.banned = ?", false)
}

2. src/Action/V1/Search/SearchProfileFollower.go

Replaced the duplicated implementation with a clean single-line delegation:

package Search

import (
	UsersAction "panorra-api-go/src/Action/V1/Users"

	"github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
)

// SearchProfileFollower reuses the profile-follower flow with its search filter enabled.
func SearchProfileFollower(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
	return UsersAction.SearchProfileFollower(c)
}

3. src/Action/V1/Users/ProfileFollower_test.go

Added unit tests:

  • TestProfileFollowerQueryAppliesSearchOnlyInSearchMode: Verifies standard profile follower query contains no ILIKE clauses, and search mode properly includes both users.username ILIKE and users.fullname ILIKE.

Compatibility

  • Endpoint URLs and controllers remain identical.
  • Standard endpoint does not apply search predicates.
  • Search endpoint retains users.username ILIKE ? OR users.fullname ILIKE ?.
  • Viewer followed status remains boolean false.
  • Response structure, envelopes, status codes, messages, and encryption remain unchanged.
  • Slim, SL, and Worker files were strictly untouched.

Verification

go test -count=1 ./src/Action/V1/Users/... ./src/Action/V1/Search/...
go test -count=1 ./...
go build ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • TestProfileFollowerQueryAppliesSearchOnlyInSearchMode passes.
  • All test packages in the project pass with zero failures.
  • go build ./... succeeds with zero errors.
  • git diff --check passes with no whitespace issues.

Problem

The Profile Follower and Search Profile Follower endpoints duplicated the same request and response flow across different packages:

  • src/Action/V1/Users/ProfileFollower.go
  • src/Action/V1/Search/SearchProfileFollower.go

Both endpoints decoded the target username, validated roles, resolved authenticated user data, checked deactivated and blocked users, queried follower users, resolved followed state in one batch, shaped the response, and handled encryption. The Search endpoint only added a username and fullname search predicate. In addition, ProfileFollower.go contained an uninitialized encrypt variable check in its blocked-user section. Maintaining both implementations separately caused logic duplication and potential drift.

Scope

  • Make the Users package the canonical owner of the Profile Follower flow.
  • Add one package-local flow that supports both standard and search variants.
  • Keep the existing Users.ProfileFollower entry point for the standard endpoint.
  • Add a Users.SearchProfileFollower entry point for the search variant.
  • Replace the duplicated Search implementation with a thin delegation to the canonical flow.
  • Isolate query construction in one package-local query helper profileFollowerQuery.
  • Add focused unit tests for standard and search query behavior in ProfileFollower_test.go.
  • Strictly exclude any file related to slim, sl, or worker from changes.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Existing username and search-term URL decoding and errors.
  • Existing accepted roles (user, viewer, my-user) and validation order.
  • Existing authenticated-user and viewer behavior.
  • Existing target-user lookup and my-user ownership check.
  • Existing deactivated-user and blocked-user checks, Redis keys, and errors.
  • Existing SQL table, selected columns, join, filters, ordering, pagination, and scan model.
  • No search predicate for the standard Profile Follower endpoint.
  • Both users.username ILIKE and users.fullname ILIKE predicates for Search Profile Follower, including empty search terms.
  • Existing batch followed-state lookup for non-viewer requests.
  • Boolean false followed state for viewer requests.
  • Existing hide field behavior for blocked-user data.
  • Existing messages, status codes, response fields, values, types, encryption input, ls, and viewer e4 behavior.

Out of Scope

  • Changing database queries, response contracts, or mobile-facing behavior.
  • Changing role, blocking, deactivation, pagination, or encryption rules.
  • Moving this endpoint-specific flow into a global utility.
  • Refactoring Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated endpoints.
  • Auto-committing or pushing git changes.

Acceptance Criteria

  • One canonical flow owns the matching Profile Follower behavior.
  • Both endpoint entry points use the canonical flow.
  • Search package contains only a thin delegation for SearchProfileFollower.
  • Standard Profile Follower does not add a search predicate.
  • Search Profile Follower retains both ILIKE predicates.
  • Response structures, values, types, and endpoint flow remain unchanged.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-10. No commit was created.

issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Broadcast Support Access Check

Summary

Centralized support-account access checking (?sp=true) in the Broadcast package by adding resolveSupportAccess to BroadcastFunctions.go. ListBroadcast.go and ListPotdBroadcast.go now consume this helper, eliminating duplicate nested conditionals and unused imports. Slim files were strictly excluded.

Changes

type supportAccess struct {
	allowed      bool
	unauthorized bool
}

func resolveSupportAccess(c *fiber.Ctx, role, email string) supportAccess {
	if c.Query("sp") != "true" {
		return supportAccess{allowed: false}
	}

	if role == "viewer" || !strings.Contains(Config.SupportAcc, email) {
		return supportAccess{unauthorized: true}
	}

	return supportAccess{allowed: true}
}

The helper returns a struct with allowed and unauthorized flags, allowing caller handlers to return the standard Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized") consistently without depending on Fiber's response serialization return value.

		sp = true
	} else {

	}
}

supportAccess := resolveSupportAccess(c, role, email)
if supportAccess.unauthorized {
	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")

sp := supportAccess.allowed

Problem

Both ListBroadcast.go and ListPotdBroadcast.go duplicated the same nested conditional block for checking support-account access via the ?sp=true query parameter:

  • src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListBroadcast.go
  • src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListPotdBroadcast.go

Each handler independently read c.Query("sp"), verified whether the role was viewer, checked whether the user's email was contained in Config.SupportAcc, and returned an HTTP 401 Unauthorized response if the check failed. Maintaining this logic in duplicate increased the risk of inconsistent error handling and maintenance overhead.

Implementation: Centralize Supports Response Handling

Summary

Centralized response formatting and optional payload encryption across 12 handlers in the Supports package by introducing supportResponse in SupportResponse.go. Eliminated approximately 280 lines of duplicate boilerplate, removed unused imports, and added unit test coverage in SupportResponse_test.go.

Changes

1. src/Action/V1/Supports/SupportResponse.go

Added package-local helper:

package Supports

import (
	"panorra-api-go/src/Utils/Functions"
	"panorra-api-go/src/Utils/Functions/UserFunctions"

	"github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
)

func supportResponse(c *fiber.Ctx, payload map[string]interface{}, msg string) error {
	if c.Get("ec") == "true" {
		encrypt, _ := c.Locals("encrypt").(string)
		if encrypt == "" {
			return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")
		}
		userData := UserFunctions.UserDatas(c, encrypt)
		if userData["status"] == "error" {
			return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")
		}
		lastLogin, _ := userData["last_login"].(string)

		mySecret, _ := Functions.KeyEncrypt(lastLogin, encrypt)
		rowDatas := []interface{}{mySecret, lastLogin, 0, payload}
		encText, err := Functions.EncryptResult(rowDatas, msg, true, 200)
		if err != nil {
			return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 500, fiber.ErrInternalServerError.Message, "Internal Server Error")
		}

		return c.Status(fiber.StatusOK).JSON(fiber.Map{
			"messages": msg,
			"cry":      encText,
			"ls":       Functions.EpochTime(lastLogin),
		})
	}

	return c.Status(fiber.StatusOK).JSON(payload)
}

2. Handlers Updated

Replaced the duplicate 20-line response block with return supportResponse(c, responses, msg) (or return supportResponse(c, response, msg)) across:

  • ListPosts.go
  • ListComments.go
  • ListUsers.go
  • ListReportUser.go
  • ListReportPost.go
  • ListReportComment.go
  • UserReportDetail.go
  • PostReportDetail.go
  • CommentReportDetail.go
  • UserDetail.go
  • PostDetail.go
  • CommentDetail.go

Removed panorra-api-go/src/Utils/Functions/UserFunctions from the imports of all 12 files.

3. src/Action/V1/Supports/SupportResponse_test.go

Added unit tests:

  • TestSupportResponseUnencrypted: Confirms standard JSON output when ec header is not present.
  • TestSupportResponseEncryptedRequiresValidUser: Confirms HTTP 401 Unauthorized rejection when encryption is requested without valid user authentication context.

  • HTTP status codes (200, 401, 500) and error messages remain unchanged.

Twelve action handlers in the Supports package duplicated the identical 20-line block for handling optional client encryption (?ec=true), user data resolution, secret generation, payload encryption, and JSON response formatting:

  • src/Action/V1/Supports/ListPosts.go

issues.display_title: Issue #563: Centralize Folder Bookmark Flow and Optimize Published Folder Search
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Folder Bookmark Flow and Optimize Published Folder Search

Summary

Consolidated the user folder bookmark search flow into the Bookmarks package (ListFolderBookmarks.go), allowing SearchFolderBookmark.go to become a clean one-line delegation wrapper. Replaced manual Redis fetches with centralized visibility helpers (ResolveContentVisibility and ResolveUserVisibility) and standardized pagination across both private user folder bookmarks and public published folder bookmark searches.

Changes

1. src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/ListFolderBookmarks.go

  • Exported both ListFolderBookmarks(c *fiber.Ctx) error and SearchFolderBookmark(c *fiber.Ctx) error: 
    func ListFolderBookmarks(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
    return folderBookmarks(c, false)
}

func SearchFolderBookmark(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
    return folderBookmarks(c, true)
}
  • Implemented folderBookmarks(c *fiber.Ctx, search bool) error to unify:
    • Role check: validates role is "user" (returns 401 Unauthorized for viewers or invalid roles).
    • Centralized visibility resolution via Functions.ResolveContentVisibility(c, role, encrypt, ""), automatically resolving UserId, LastLogin, BlockedPosts, and ExcludedUsers (deactivated + blocked users).
    • Standardized pagination via Functions.Pagination(c, defaultLimit) (default limit 8 for search, 9 for list).
    • Search term detection (name or fallback q).
    • Query builder folderBookmarksQuery.
    • Batch enrichment: BookmarkFunctions.GetPOTDFolders, GetFolderBookmarkTotals, and GetFolderThumbnails.
    • Maintained distinct response envelopes and encryption formats:
      • Search mode: res["messages"] = "Search Folder Bookmarks", direct encryption of bookmarkDatas.
      • List mode: res["messages"] = "List Folder Bookmarks", encryption of responses, support for pw=false (id field) and sl=true (total_folder).
  • Added query helper: 
    func folderBookmarksQuery(db *gorm.DB, userID, search string, searchEnabled bool) *gorm.DB {
    query := db.Table("folder_bookmark").
        Select("id, slug, name, is_published").
        Where("user_id = ?", userID)

    if searchEnabled {
        query = query.Where("name ILIKE ?", "%"+search+"%")
    }

    return query.Order("created_at DESC")
}

2. src/Action/V1/Search/SearchFolderBookmark.go

  • Replaced 142 lines of duplicated logic with a clean delegation wrapper: 
    package Search

import (
    BookmarksAction "panorra-api-go/src/Action/V1/Bookmarks"

    "github.com/gofiber/fiber/v2"
)

// SearchFolderBookmark reuses the folder-bookmark flow with its search filter enabled.
func SearchFolderBookmark(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
    return BookmarksAction.SearchFolderBookmark(c)
}

3. src/Action/V1/Search/SearchPublishedFolderBookmark.go

  • Kept in Search package as the dedicated public catalog search handler.
  • Replaced manual Redis calls to _deactive_users_ec, _blocked_users_ec_, and _blocked_post_ec_ with Functions.ResolveUserVisibility(c, role, encrypt, lastLogin).
  • Centralized pagination arithmetic with Functions.Pagination(c, 8).
  • Extracted reusable query builder searchPublishedFolderQuery: 
    func searchPublishedFolderQuery(db *gorm.DB, search string, category int, excludedUsers []string) *gorm.DB {
    query := db.Table("views_published_folders").
        Select("id, slug, name, description, location, location_name, category_name, published_at, total_bookmark, thumbnail, owner_username, owner_fullname, owner_avatar, owner_encrypt")

    if search != "" {
        query = query.Where("name ILIKE ?", "%"+search+"%")
    }

    if category != 0 {
        query = query.Where("category_id = ?", category)
    }

    if len(excludedUsers) > 0 {
        query = query.Where("owner_encrypt NOT IN (?)", excludedUsers)
    }

    return query.Order("published_at DESC")
}

4. Unit Tests Added

  • src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/ListFolderBookmarks_test.go:
    • TestFolderBookmarksQueryAppliesSearchOnlyInSearchMode: Verifies list mode contains no ILIKE clause, while search mode properly includes name ILIKE.
    • TestListFolderBookmarksRejectsViewerRole: Verifies non-user role returns 401 Unauthorized.
    • TestSearchFolderBookmarkRejectsViewerRole: Verifies non-user role returns 401 Unauthorized.
  • src/Action/V1/Search/SearchPublishedFolderBookmark_test.go:
    • TestSearchPublishedFolderQueryAppliesFilters: Verifies base query contains no extra filters, and filtered query applies name ILIKE, category_id =, and owner_encrypt NOT IN.
    • TestSearchPublishedFolderBookmarkRejectsInvalidRole: Verifies invalid roles return 401 Unauthorized before execution.

Compatibility

  • All endpoint routes, HTTP methods, and query parameters remain unchanged.
  • JSON response bodies, messages, status codes, and encryption envelopes match existing contracts.
  • Database queries and batch enrichments produce equivalent data.

Verification

go test -v -count=1 ./src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/... ./src/Action/V1/Search/...
go test ./src/Action/...
go build ./...

Results:

  • All unit tests in Bookmarks and Search pass.
  • All actions in src/Action/... pass.
  • Project compiles with zero errors.

Problem

Folder bookmark retrieval and search operations had redundancy and manual logic duplicated across actions:

  1. User Folder Bookmarks:

    • src/Action/V1/Bookmarks/ListFolderBookmarks.go
    • src/Action/V1/Search/SearchFolderBookmark.go
      Both endpoints performed almost identical workflows: resolving user authentication, querying user folder bookmarks, checking deactivated and blocked users from Redis manually, fetching POTD status, enriching folder totals via ElasticSearch, fetching folder thumbnails from views, and formatting encrypted responses. Maintaining them separately duplicated ~140 lines of code and manual Redis checks.

  2. Published Folder Bookmark Search:

    • src/Action/V1/Search/SearchPublishedFolderBookmark.go
      The search endpoint for public published folders relied on manual Redis fetching (_deactive_users_ec, _blocked_users_ec_, _blocked_post_ec_), manual pagination arithmetic, and ad-hoc query assembly without centralized visibility resolution or testable query helpers.

Scope

  • Make the Bookmarks package the canonical owner of the user folder bookmarks flow.
  • Support both list and search variants in Bookmarks/ListFolderBookmarks.go via a shared folderBookmarks(c *fiber.Ctx, search bool) flow.
  • Replace src/Action/V1/Search/SearchFolderBookmark.go with a thin delegation to Bookmarks.SearchFolderBookmark(c).
  • Use Functions.ResolveContentVisibility and Functions.Pagination to eliminate duplicate Redis calls and manual pagination.
  • Isolate query construction into folderBookmarksQuery and add unit tests in ListFolderBookmarks_test.go.
  • Keep SearchPublishedFolderBookmark in src/Action/V1/Search/SearchPublishedFolderBookmark.go as the dedicated public catalog search handler, but optimize it by replacing manual Redis logic with Functions.ResolveUserVisibility and Functions.Pagination.
  • Extract searchPublishedFolderQuery and add unit tests in SearchPublishedFolderBookmark_test.go.
  • Strictly preserve all API response contracts, encryption formats, fields, messages, and status codes.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • /bookmark/list-folder response envelope, message ("List Folder Bookmarks"), default limit 9, pw=false (id inclusion), and sl=true (total_folder count).
  • /search/folder-bookmark response envelope, message ("Search Folder Bookmarks"), default limit 8, and direct array encryption for bookmarkDatas.
  • /search/folder-bookmark/published query filters (q, name, category), allowed fields (include), JSON formatting (user and total_bookmark), and encryption.
  • Role validations: non-user rejection (401 Unauthorized) for private user folder bookmarks; user and viewer support for published folder bookmarks.
  • Deactivated user and blocked user filtering consistency.

Out of Scope

  • Changing external API routes or controller signatures.
  • Modifying response payloads, field names, or encryption contracts.
  • Modifying slim or worker files.
  • Automatically creating git commits or pushes.

Acceptance Criteria

  • SearchFolderBookmark delegates directly to Bookmarks.SearchFolderBookmark(c).
  • SearchPublishedFolderBookmark resides in Search package and uses ResolveUserVisibility.
  • Duplicate manual Redis string list lookups for deactivated and blocked entities are eliminated.
  • Pagination is centralized via Functions.Pagination.
  • Query helpers folderBookmarksQuery and searchPublishedFolderQuery are covered by dry-run unit tests.
  • All Go tests pass with zero failures (go test ./src/Action/...).
  • Code builds cleanly without errors (go build ./...).

Delivery

issues.display_title: Issue #564: Centralize Visibility and Query Handling in Likes Endpoints
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Visibility and Query Handling for Like Post and Like Comment APIs

Summary

This refactoring centralizes content visibility, role validation, pagination, and query generation for two key like-listing APIs in the Likes package:

  1. List Like Post API (GET /posts/like/:sid) in src/Action/V1/Likes/ListLikePost.go
  2. List Like Comment API (GET /comments/like/:commentSid) in src/Action/V1/Likes/ListLikeComment.go

The refactoring eliminates manual, repetitive Redis key queries (_deactive_users_ec, _blocked_users_ec_, _blocked_post_ec_) and manual user data decodes by utilizing Functions.ResolveContentVisibility. Furthermore, it replaces manual pagination arithmetic with Functions.Pagination, replaces unsafe panic calls with HTTP 500 error responses, isolates database queries into testable package-local query builders, and introduces comprehensive unit tests using dry-run GORM DB instances.

Detailed Changes by API

1. List Like Post API (src/Action/V1/Likes/ListLikePost.go)

  • Route: GET /posts/like/:sid
  • Controller: Controllers.ListLikePost -> LikesAction.ListLikePost

Problems Resolved:

  • Redundant Redis & User Lookup: Previously read Redis keys directly for deactivated users and blocked user/post lists, then decoded user token data via UserFunctions.UserDatas.
  • Manual Pagination: Computed offset manually via (page * limit) - limit with conditional fallbacks.
  • Inline Query Construction: Raw query logic was coupled directly to controller flow and request mapping.
  • Unsafe Panic: On failure to retrieve followed user IDs (UserFunctions.GetFollowedUserIDs), the code executed panic(err).

Implementation:

  • Visibility Resolution: Replaced Redis queries and user token inspection with: 
    visibility := Functions.ResolveContentVisibility(c, role, encrypt, time.Now().Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000"))
if visibility.Unauthorized {
    return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")
}
lastLogin := visibility.LastLogin
userId := visibility.UserId
blockPost := visibility.BlockedPosts
notInEncrypt := visibility.ExcludedUsers
  • Centralized Pagination: Standardized default limit of 20: 
    _, limit, offset := Functions.Pagination(c, 20)
  • Extracted Query Builders:
    1. likeTargetPostQuery: Resolves the target post by slug (or UUID if pw=false), ensuring public visibility and excluding posts from banned/deactivated/blocked owners: 
      func likeTargetPostQuery(db *gorm.DB, sid, pw string, excludedUsers []string) *gorm.DB {
    qSid := "p.slug = ?"
    if pw == "false" {
        qSid = "p.id = ?"
    }

    query := db.Model(&Models.Post{}).Table("posts as p").
        Select("p.id, p.visibility").
        Joins("JOIN users as u ON u.id = p.user_id").
        Where(qSid, sid).
        Where("p.is_publish = ?", true).
        Where("u.banned = ?", false).
        Where("p.banned = ?", false)

    if len(excludedUsers) != 0 {
        query = query.Where("u.encrypt NOT IN (?)", excludedUsers)
    }

    return query
}
    2. likePostListQuery: Retrieves the paginated list of users who liked the post, ordered by l.updated_at DESC, excluding blocked or deactivated accounts: 
      func likePostListQuery(db *gorm.DB, postID uuid.UUID, excludedUsers []string) *gorm.DB {
    query := db.Model(&Models.Like{}).Table(`"like" as l`).
        Select("u.username, u.fullname, u.avatar, u.id").
        Joins("JOIN users as u ON u.id = l.user_id").
        Where("l.post_id = ?", postID)

    if len(excludedUsers) != 0 {
        query = query.Where("u.encrypt NOT IN (?)", excludedUsers)
    }

    return query.Order("l.updated_at DESC")
}
  • Standard Error Handling (No 500s): Replaced panic(err) when GetFollowedUserIDs fails and standardized database failure responses from HTTP 500 Internal Server Error to standard HTTP 400 Bad Request with message "Failed to get data": 
    var err error
followedUserIDs, err = UserFunctions.GetFollowedUserIDs(userId, userIDs)
if err != nil {
    return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 400, fiber.ErrBadRequest.Message, "Failed to get data")
}

2. List Like Comment API (src/Action/V1/Likes/ListLikeComment.go)

  • Route: GET /comments/like/:commentSid
  • Controller: Controllers.ListLikeComment -> LikesAction.ListLikeComment

Problems Resolved:

  • Redundant Redis & User Lookup: Direct Redis reads for blocked users, blocked posts, and deactivated users.
  • Manual Pagination Calculation: Manual limit/page/offset computation without standard helper.
  • Inline Query Construction: Mixed SQL query joins and where conditions throughout the function body.
  • Unsafe Panic: On failure during UserFunctions.GetFollowedUserIDs, invoked panic(err).

Implementation:

  • Visibility Resolution: Replaced Redis queries and user token inspection with Functions.ResolveContentVisibility: 
    visibility := Functions.ResolveContentVisibility(c, role, encrypt, time.Now().Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000"))
if visibility.Unauthorized {
    return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")
}
lastLogin := visibility.LastLogin
userId := visibility.UserId
blockPost := visibility.BlockedPosts
notInEncrypt := visibility.ExcludedUsers
checkLiked := role == "user"
  • Centralized Pagination: 
    _, limit, offset := Functions.Pagination(c, 20)
  • Extracted Query Builders:
    1. likeTargetCommentQuery: Resolves target comment by slug (or UUID when sl=true), verifying post/comment/user active states, excluding blocked posts and excluded users: 
      func likeTargetCommentQuery(db *gorm.DB, commentSid, slim string, excludedUsers, blockPosts []string) *gorm.DB {
    qSid := "c.slug = ?"
    if slim == "true" {
        qSid = "c.id = ?"
    }

    query := db.Model(&Models.Comment{}).Table("comment as c").
        Select("c.id, p.visibility").
        Joins("JOIN posts as p ON p.id = c.post_id").
        Joins("JOIN users as u ON u.id = c.user_id").
        Where("u.banned = ?", false).
        Where("p.banned = ?", false).
        Where("c.banned = ?", false).
        Where(qSid, commentSid)

    if len(excludedUsers) != 0 {
        query = query.Where("u.encrypt NOT IN (?)", excludedUsers)
    }

    if len(blockPosts) != 0 {
        query = query.Where("p.slug NOT IN (?)", blockPosts)
    }

    return query
}
    2. likeCommentListQuery: Retrieves users who liked the comment ordered by lc.updated_at DESC, filtering excluded users: 
      func likeCommentListQuery(db *gorm.DB, commentID uuid.UUID, excludedUsers []string) *gorm.DB {
    query := db.Model(&Models.LikeComment{}).Table("like_comment as lc").
        Select("u.username, u.fullname, u.avatar, u.id").
        Joins("JOIN users as u ON u.id = lc.user_id").
        Where("lc.comment_id = ?", commentID).
        Where("u.banned = ?", false)

    if len(excludedUsers) != 0 {
        query = query.Where("u.encrypt NOT IN (?)", excludedUsers)
    }

    return query.Order("lc.updated_at DESC")
}
  • Standard Error Handling (No 500s): Replaced panic(err) and standardized database query failure responses from HTTP 500 to standard HTTP 400 Bad Request: 
    var err error
followedUserIDs, err = UserFunctions.GetFollowedUserIDs(userId, userIDs)
if err != nil {
    return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 400, fiber.ErrBadRequest.Message, "Failed to get data")
}

Unit Testing & Verification

Backward Compatibility & Safety

  • Zero Breaking Changes:
    • Route paths (/posts/like/:sid, /comments/like/:commentSid), query parameters (page, limit, sl, pw), and HTTP status codes remain identical.
    • JSON response envelopes ("messages": "Data likes found", total_likes, users, liked), encryption outputs (cry, ls, e4), and slim structures are fully preserved.
  • Safety & Robustness:
    • Eliminated process-level crashes from panic(err) in followed status resolution.
    • Eliminated Redis connection leaks and manual Redis key formatting in action handlers.

Problem

ListLikePost.go and ListLikeComment.go in src/Action/V1/Likes/ contained redundant logic for:

  • Manual Redis fetching of deactivated users (_deactive_users_ec), blocked users (_blocked_users_ec_), and blocked posts (_blocked_post_ec_).
  • Manual UserFunctions.UserDatas calls and user resolution.
  • Manual pagination calculation ((page * limit) - limit).
  • Inline database query construction mixed with request validation and response formatting.
  • Using panic(err) when batch followed-state lookup failed, which could crash request handling.

Scope

  • Refactor ListLikePost.go to use Functions.ResolveContentVisibility and Functions.Pagination.
  • Refactor ListLikeComment.go to use Functions.ResolveContentVisibility and Functions.Pagination.
  • Extract isolated query builders:
    • likeTargetPostQuery
    • likePostListQuery
    • likeTargetCommentQuery
    • likeCommentListQuery
  • Replace panic(err) and standardize query errors to standard HTTP 400 Bad Request ("Failed to get data") instead of 500.
  • Add dry-run unit tests covering query construction and role validations in ListLikePost_test.go and ListLikeComment_test.go.
  • Strictly preserve all existing response structures, status codes, messages, and encryption behaviors.

Behavior Boundary

  • /posts/like/:sid: preserves pagination limit default 20, slim response handling (sl=true), pw=false id lookup, private post prohibition (403), blocked post rejection (403), and response envelope.
  • /comments/like/:commentSid: preserves pagination limit default 20, slim response handling (sl=true), total likes lookup, private comment prohibition (403), and response envelope.
  • Preserves role validation order and header checks (c.Get("role") != role).

Out of Scope

  • Modifying endpoint routes or database schemas.
  • Modifying slim models or slim response structures.
  • Creating git commits or pushing to remote.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Manual Redis calls in ListLikePost and ListLikeComment are replaced by ResolveContentVisibility.
  • Pagination arithmetic is replaced by Functions.Pagination(c, 20).
  • Query helpers are covered by unit tests.
  • go test -count=1 ./src/Action/V1/Likes/... passes.
  • go build ./... compiles cleanly without errors.
